diagnostic_evidence.quote: The matrix $a = \kappa^{-1}\cdot\mu$ in the denominator is invertible and $\mathrm{rank}(a) = N+1$.
Therefore the numerator of $R(z)$ is a polynomial $P_{N, N+1}(z)$ of degree $N-1$.
It follows that $R(z)$ is the $(N, N+1)$-Pad\'{e} approximation $R_{N, N+1}(z)$ of $\exp(z)$.

issues.failure_explanation: If a is full rank N+1, det(I-za) has degree N+1, not N. If rank(a-1w^T)=N, the numerator det(I-za+z1w^T) has degree N, not N-1. Moreover, degree/rank alone does not show that R(z) has the Taylor expansion of exp(z) through order 2N+1, which is required to identify R as the (N,N+1)-Padé approximation.
